verdict.rationale: uv documents aggressive caching that avoids re-downloading and re-building dependencies already accessed in prior runs, backed by a global deduplicating cache. That covers the core of reusing cached built artifacts instead of compiling again. The evidence never explicitly addresses installing prebuilt binary wheels instead of source builds, and one community report says uvx sometimes re-downloads dependencies it just fetched. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of prebuilt wheel (binary) preference and installation from the cache, detail on how built wheels are cached and reused across environments, and independent hands-on corroboration that source compilation is avoided.

support.subject: As a developer, I can install prebuilt binary packages from a cache instead of compiling from source

citations.quote: uv uses aggressive caching to avoid re-downloading (and re-building) dependencies that have already been accessed in prior runs.
Disk-space efficient, with a [global cache](concepts/cache/) for dependency deduplication.
